one_sentence: Rain-associated acoustic expansion is recurrent re-expression of a latent species-by-site chorus network; dynamic soil-water change supplies an additional broadly transportable hydric-state axis, while historical local chorus use supplies the spatial template and realized activation depth drives the matrix anomaly.

acoustic_boundary_crossing.conclusion: Rain-associated change includes emergence of overlapping/full choruses, not merely louder already-active cells or CI1-only detections.

recurrent_local_template.conclusion: Previously used own-species physical sites are preferentially re-expressed. Generic site quality and sampling opportunity are insufficient explanations.
recurrent_local_template.unresolved: Cannot distinguish persistent local population from persistent species-specific microhabitat suitability.

hydric_state.conclusion: Wet-minus-dry soil-water change is the strongest tested environmental correlate of strong chorus recruitment and transports across routes, periods, robust subsets and state omissions.

hydric_change_not_binary_gate.conclusion: Relative soil-water change is more consistent than an absolute threshold, but positive soil wetting is not a necessary on/off condition for the rain-recency signal. Rain recency and soil hydric state retain partly distinct information.

spatial_depth.conclusion: The matrix anomaly is activation depth into third-and-later stops, overwhelmingly at substantial chorus intensity; special stop placement is unnecessary after species identity and realized depth are fixed.

hydric_plus_template_depth.conclusion: Historical template breadth and soil-water change independently predict post-activation depth in the full sample. The full-sample interaction is not supported, so a largely additive two-axis model is safer than a universal multiplicative gate.

protocol_robustness.conclusion: The soil-water association is not confined to comparisons wholly inside the 0-3-day survey target window; the both-outside subset is small and imprecise.

falsified_or_insufficient: simple chorus facilitation to dry-active stops
positive soil-wetting sign as necessary gate
generic site productivity instead of own-species site history
special spatial placement conditional on realized activation depth

within_NAAMP.status: strong pooled generality with local heterogeneity

cross_continent.reason: No effort-complete comparable multi-site species x site matrix has been identified; available AnuraSet site tests do not reproduce the prefixed threshold-dominance rule.

best_supported_statement: Recent rain is associated with re-expression of a persistent species-specific local chorus network. Among tested environmental variables, wet-minus-dry soil-water change provides the strongest broadly transportable hydric-state information and independently predicts both substantial chorus recruitment and the spatial depth of activated taxa. Rain recency is not fully reducible to a binary soil-wetting gate.

mechanistic_ceiling.unresolved_population_vs_habitat: Persistent local populations versus persistent species-specific microhabitat suitability cannot be separated from these acoustic observations.
mechanistic_ceiling.unresolved_hydric_route: ERA5 soil water cannot distinguish frog hydration from breeding-site water availability/inundation or correlated hydric processes.

stop_rule: Do not add more post-readback NAAMP regression variants unless they test a qualitatively new falsifiable alternative. Next decisive evidence requires direct hydrology/body-hydration or individual-level data, or an independent effort-complete acoustic matrix.
